prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c2s2: Limits are defined on functions; precalc intro limits provide intuition.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c2s3: Limit laws evaluate limits defined previously.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c2s5: Epsilon-delta proofs formalize the limit concept; not required for applications.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s1: The derivative is defined as a limit; precalc derivative intro helps.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s2: Derivative-as-a-function extends the pointwise derivative definition.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s3: Differentiation rules operate on the derivative function.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s4: Applied rates interpret the derivative in context.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s5: Trig derivatives need trig functions and basic differentiation rules.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s6: The chain rule extends the power, product, and quotient rules.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s7: Inverse-function derivatives use inverses and the chain rule.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s8: Implicit differentiation applies the chain rule to implicitly defined curves.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c3s9: Exponential and logarithmic derivatives need those functions and the chain rule.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s1: Related rates problems require derivatives and the chain rule.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s2: Linear approximation uses the derivative at a point.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s3: Finding extrema uses the first derivative.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s4: Mean Value Theorem connects continuity, differentiability, and the derivative.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s5: Curve sketching uses first and second derivative tests built on critical points.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s6: Limits at infinity and asymptotes extend limit evaluation and graph analysis.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s7: Optimization sets up and solves extrema problems; does not require L'Hopital's Rule.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s8: L'Hopital's Rule evaluates indeterminate limits; requires derivatives and limits at infinity, not optimization.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s9: Newton's Method iterates using the derivative; independent of optimization or L'Hopital.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c4s10: Antiderivatives reverse differentiation rules, including exp/log derivatives.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s1: Riemann sums use limits and antiderivative intuition.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s2: The definite integral is defined as a limit of Riemann sums.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s3: The Fundamental Theorem connects differentiation and the definite integral.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s4: Integration formulas and net change apply FTC and antiderivatives.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s5: u-substitution is the chain rule in reverse.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s6: Integrals of exponentials and logarithms use those functions and basic integration.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c5s7: Inverse trig integrals use inverse trig functions and substitution.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s1: Area between curves is computed with definite integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s2: Volume by slicing integrates cross-sectional areas.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s3: Shell method is an alternative volume technique; needs definite integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s4: Arc length integrals use substitution and the chain rule.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s5: Work and density applications set up definite integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s6: Centers of mass extend physical integration applications.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s7: Defines ln and e via integrals; builds on FTC and log/exp integration.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s8: Exponential growth/decay models use exponential functions and integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-1:c6s9: Hyperbolic functions are introduced with their derivatives and integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c1s1: Area approximation continues Calc 1 Riemann-sum ideas.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c1s2: Definite integrals continue Calc 1 integral definition.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c1s4: Integration formulas and net change continue Calc 1.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c1s6: Exp/log integrals continue Calc 1 exp/log integration.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c2s1: Area between curves continues Calc 1 applications.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c2s3: Shell method continues Calc 1 volume techniques.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c2s6: Centers of mass continue physical applications.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c2s7: Integral definitions of ln/e continue Calc 1.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c2s9: Hyperbolic calculus continues Calc 1 hyperbolic functions.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c3s1: Integration by parts needs substitution fluency and product-rule intuition.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c3s2: Trig integrals need trig functions and substitution.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c3s3: Trig substitution uses trig identities and integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c3s4: Partial-fraction integrals need algebraic partial fractions.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c3s5: Other strategies choose among parts, trig, and partial fractions.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c3s7: Improper integrals need FTC and limits at infinity.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c4s1: Differential equations relate derivatives to functions.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c4s3: Separable equations solve DEs by integration/substitution.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c4s4: Logistic equation specializes separable growth models.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c4s5: First-order linear DEs extend separable techniques.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c5s1: Sequences need precalc sequences and limit language.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c5s2: Infinite series are limits of sequence partial sums.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c5s3: Integral test connects series to improper integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c5s4: Comparison tests use series convergence concepts.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c5s5: Alternating series are a special series test family.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c5s6: Ratio/root tests are further series tests.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c6s1: Power series are series of functions needing convergence tests.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c6s2: Power-series properties build on power-series definition.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c6s3: Taylor series use derivatives and power series.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c6s4: Working with Taylor series applies Taylor expansions.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c7s1: Parametric equations continue precalc parametrics with calculus readiness.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c7s3: Polar coordinates continue precalc polar with trig.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c7s4: Polar area/arc length integrate in polar coordinates.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-2:c7s5: Polar conics continue precalc polar conic sections.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c1s1: Parametrics review continues Calc 2 parametric equations.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c2s4: Cross product is a 3D vector operation.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c2s5: Lines and planes use vector operations.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c2s6: Quadric surfaces extend conic ideas to 3D.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c2s7: Cylindrical/spherical coords combine 3D vectors with polar ideas.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c3s1: Vector-valued functions map parameters to vectors/curves.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c3s2: Calculus of vector functions uses componentwise derivatives.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c3s4: Motion in space interprets vector derivatives as velocity/acceleration.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c4s1: Functions of several variables extend single-variable functions to R^n.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c4s3: Partial derivatives differentiate in one variable at a time.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c4s5: Multivariable chain rule extends single-variable chain rule.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c4s6: Gradient/directional derivatives use partials and dot products.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c4s8: Lagrange multipliers constrain multivariable extrema with gradients.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c5s1: Double integrals over rectangles extend definite integrals to 2D.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c5s2: General-region double integrals extend rectangular ones.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c5s4: Triple integrals extend double integrals to 3D.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c5s5: Cylindrical/spherical triple integrals use those coordinate systems.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c5s6: Moments/centers of mass use multiple integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c5s7: Change of variables generalizes polar/cylindrical substitutions.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s1: Vector fields assign vectors to points in space.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s2: Line integrals integrate along curves in vector fields.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s3: Conservative fields connect line integrals to gradients.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s4: Green's Theorem relates line integrals to double integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s5: Divergence and curl are differential operators on vector fields.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s6: Surface integrals integrate over surfaces in fields.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s7: Stokes' Theorem relates curl to surface/line integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c6s8: Divergence Theorem relates divergence to flux integrals.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c7s1: Second-order linear DEs extend first-order DE methods.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c7s2: Nonhomogeneous equations build on homogeneous second-order theory.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c7s3: Applications use second-order DE solution methods.
prerequisite_reasons.calculus-volume-3:c7s4: Series solutions of DEs use power/Taylor series.
